articles.title: America, Satan Called and He Wants His Baby Brother Back
articles.author: Desi Cortez
articles.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Stephen Miller is a hate monger; he promotes racism and hostility, and he is the pillar of the MAGA world who’s pulling Trump’s strings in the White House I’d venture to guess the Devil understated their relationship. Stephen Miller could be Lucifer’s identical twin, separated at birth, raised among mortals, and dispatched to Washington to finish what Hell couldn't accomplish alone. I’m serious! Something wicked this way comes In my opinion, Miller is among the most ominous, creepy, dangerous, morally repugnant figures to emerge from the Land of MAGA. His hostility toward immigrants , fixation on who belongs, and apparent indifference to suffering remind me less of an American statesman than Joseph Goebbels, Adolf Hitler’s propaganda minister, who transformed prejudice into Nazi patriotism, lies into doctrine, and persecution into public duty. Different century, different uniform, but the political echoes are unmistakable. I’m not saying history repeats itself word for word. Related: Goebbels’s Ghost and Miller’s Dream of a “Unified Reich” But I sure as hell hear it rhyming. Those echoes should make grown Americans sick to their stomachs. We have seen what happens when government first teaches its people whom to despise. This modern merchant of misery now occupies corridors where Abraham Lincoln struggled to preserve an imperfect Union, and Franklin Roosevelt confronted fascism, including the homegrown sympathies of prominent Americans like Henry Ford and Charles Lindbergh. Here’s what should scare the living hell out of anybody with a functioning conscience: I don’t believe Donald Trump is the mastermind of this nightmare. I believe Stephen Miller is. Remember Pinky and the Brain , those laboratory rats endlessly plotting world domination? Miller is the Brain, the calculating schemer who knows how to exploit power. Trump is Pinky, or Orangie, the loudmouthed accomplice who mistakes his mountainous ego for intelligence. Orangie believes he’s issuing orders while the Brain quietly drafts instructions. Trump supplies the spectacle, presidential seal, and vanity. Miller supplies the ideology, targets, and calculated cruelty . It’s a bargain between a man addicted to applause and another addicted to the machinery of power. That’s what makes this frightening. Trump’s hatred is theatrical. Miller’s is methodical. Trump bellows about enemies; Miller helps build machinery to pursue them. Trump wants applause; Miller wants policies that outlive the cheering mob. One is a political arsonist. The other studies blueprints, deciding which exits to lock before the fire starts. On November 6, Trump named Miller White House chief of staff, effective November 9. The man I suspect writes the instructions will now supervise the staff. Apparently, political arson earns a promotion. What haunts me isn’t simply what Miller has said or done. It’s what further barbarities a man with his convictions might pursue when handed extraordinary power, surrounded by obedient officials, and protected by a president whose moral compass points permanently toward himself. Congress and the press ought to be on this fellow’s tail like bloodhounds tracking a stolen ham. May the gods have mercy on America. The most dangerous man in the White House may not sit behind the Resolute Desk. He may stand beside it, whispering into the president’s ear, plotting who belongs in America and who should suffer for believing they do. Seven episodes explain why I refuse to mistake Miller’s influence for ordinary corporate Republican conservatism. The White Nationalist Reading Club In 2015 and 2016, Miller emailed Breitbart editors material from VDARE, a website associated with white nationalism. He recommended The Camp of the Saints , a novel portraying nonwhite refugees overrunning Western civilization. Imagine choosing bedtime reading from the white supremacist bargain bin, then helping write immigration policy for a nation of immigrants. His defenders can debate his intentions; the emails establish what he circulated. Bigotry doesn’t become harmless by acquiring a government email address. Nor does a poisonous worldview become respectable because somebody types it into a memorandum and calls it policy. The Confederate Flag Sympathy Department After white supremacist Dylann Roof slaughtered nine Black worshippers inside Charleston’s Mother Emanuel AME Church in 2015, officers reportedly bought their captured killer Burger King. Heaven forbid the poor little mass murderer should go hungry. Nine innocent people lay dead in their church, yet someone made sure the killer got a meal. Ain’t that a bitch?! Meanwhile, retailers began removing Confederate merchandise, and Miller’s leaked emails showed him pushing back by comparing that merchandise with communist products still sold in stores. Consider the level of Vulcan inability to “feel,” the moral bankruptcy: Nine Black people were murdered while worshipping God, and Miller was busy defending the commercial dignity of Confederate symbols. What a talent for locating the wounded feelings of a flag… while grieving families remain inconveniently human. Apparently Confederate merchandise deserves a more passionate defense than Black humanity. Am I lying? The Muslim Ban Salesman Miller helped craft Trump’s first administration’s travel restrictions affecting predominantly Muslim countries. The administration called it national security; the courts fought over successive versions, and the Supreme Court upheld a revised one in 2018. Miller insisted the revisions preserved the underlying policy. When “religious discrimination” is the accusation, changing the wrapping paper doesn’t end the argument. Apparently, Lady Liberty needed a bouncer, and Miller volunteered, knocking folks down to get the opportunity, the privilege to inspect the guest list. 4. The Child Separation Accountant. In 2018, the administration’s zero-tolerance policy separated thousands of migrant children from parents. Miller defended the approach as simple. Simple! That describes choosing coffee or tea, not a terrified child crying for a mother vanished behind federal procedures. Officials called it enforcing immigration law. Families experienced government hands reaching across a parent’s arms and taking a child away. If that doesn’t chill your blood, check your pulse. Children don’t give a damn about presidential approval ratings. They want their mothers, their fathers, their homes. The American-Only Preacher At Trump’s October 2024 Madison Square Garden rally, Miller declared, “America is for Americans and Americans only.” On a discount flag, that might pass for patriotism. Amid speeches portraying migrants as threats, it resurrected America’s poisonous question: Who counts as American? A nation built by Indigenous peoples, enslaved Africans, and immigrants hardly needs another government official handing out certificates of belonging according to his preferred bloodlines and cultural tastes. The Three Thousand Arrests Man In 2025, Miller pushed ICE toward 3,000 arrests daily , according to Reuters and Axios. Not 3,000 dangerous criminals specifically. Three thousand arrests. Numbers. Quotas. Human beings reduced to production targets, as though deportation were a warehouse chasing quarterly bonuses. Officials say enforcement protects public safety. But when the scoreboard becomes the mission, justice and arithmetic start looking suspiciously interchangeable. You don’t have to be a genius to recognize the danger when liberty becomes a numbers game. The Birthright Citizenship Undertaker Miller championed Trump’s attempt to restrict birthright citizenship for children born on American soil. After the Supreme Court rejected that effort in June 2026, he complained that any interpretation requiring a nation to “suicide your civilization” must be wrong. Imagine that: newborn babies reclassified as threats to civilization , the Constitution treated as an irritating suggestion, and citizenship discussed like country-club membership controlled by inherited privilege. Fourteenth Amendment? Apparently, to Miller, fourteen is just an unlucky number. Seven Questions That Ought to Make Washington Sweat Now, after weighing this record, I have seven questions for investigators and a federal grand jury. Not seven convictions. Seven questions. I want the files opened, the witnesses sworn, and the facts dragged into daylight. If nothing criminal happened, establish that. If laws were broken, let the evidence point toward the guilty, however expensive their suits. Let us be clear about the stakes. This is not a demand that prosecutors manufacture a case to satisfy my temper. It is a demand that powerful men answer questions ordinary citizens never get to dodge, with lawyers present, records preserved, and excuses stripped of their polished Washington wrapping. Not exactly an unreasonable request. Who had their rights trampled? Were people unlawfully detained, mistreated, or punished, and did Miller knowingly help make it happen? An official title isn’t a magic shield, and the presidential signature isn’t holy water capable of washing a civil-rights violation clean. Who worked together to do it? Did officials privately agree to deny people their constitutional rights? If so, bring out the emails, not another smiling spokesman explaining that everybody meant well. I’ve heard more convincing excuses from children standing beside broken windows. Who thought federal judges were optional? Did anybody deliberately defy binding court orders on detention or deportation? If Miller was legally bound by an order and deliberately violated it, investigate. Courtrooms aren’t suggestion boxes, regardless of how many presidential portraits hang nearby. Who cooked the government books? Did anyone conspire to obstruct lawful government work through dishonesty? There’s a difference between hardball politics and rigging the game. Taxpayers didn’t hire a traveling three-card monte dealer to run the federal government. Who lied when the questions got serious? Did officials knowingly give material falsehoods to federal investigators? Political speeches can be stuffed with nonsense without automatically becoming crimes. But lies in a covered federal investigation are another matter. Suddenly the microphones are off, and somebody wants receipts. Who made the evidence disappear? Were records about families, arrests, or deportations altered or destroyed to obstruct investigation? Search the emails, preserve the files, and follow the missing documents. Government business shouldn’t vanish like socks in a dryer. Who leaned on the witnesses? Did anyone threaten employees, pressure subordinates to hide evidence, or coach witnesses into falsehoods? Let the officers, lawyers, and civil servants speak. If the policy was legal, honest testimony ought to be its best friend, not its worst nightmare. No, outrage isn’t evidence, and despicable politics aren’t automatically felonies. Criminal charges require proof of specific acts and intent; old allegations may face time limits. But neither should government power come with a lifetime pass against scrutiny. Investigate first. Let facts, not fury, decide the charges. That isn’t vengeance. It’s the minimum a republic owes its citizens. What barbarities might come next? Who knows what this political operator is capable of? The pattern deserves scrutiny: inflammatory rhetoric, punitive policy, and a determination to shrink the definition of an American. Related: The Politics of the Abyss: MAGA, Moral Rot, and the Struggle for the Future I won’t claim every other white man is Stephen Miller. That would be the kind of sweeping indictment I reject. But every American applauding this record while calling it law and order ought to examine what that applause supports. Cruelty doesn’t become citizenship merely because enough people cheer. Ordinary Americans have been warned repeatedly about surrendering their judgment and power to the powerful. Yet every generation produces citizens willing to call their neighbor’s suffering necessary, efficient, or patriotic. The question isn’t whether Miller might propose another cruelty. It’s how many respectable people will applaud, look away, or whisper that somebody probably had it coming. When subpoenas arrive, I want sworn answers, not sermons treating the Constitution as optional reading. Satan can keep his phone on. Washington has apparently extended his brother’s contract.

articles.title: More Pressure Needed to STOP the Trump EGO Arch
articles.author: Ann Wright
articles.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Despite 9.5 hours of citizen testimony from 131 persons about construction of President Trump’s massive 250-foot EGO arch with 99.9% of the testimony to STOP the arch, the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) voted 8 to 4 to allow construction. The 8 who voted for the Arch are Trump loyalists and were appointed by Trump. Over 100,000 written comments opposing the Arch have been sent to the NCPC. The plan to build it was rushed and skirted legal procedures and funding requirements under Title 40 U.S.C. § 8106. Immediately after the vote that took place after 10pm on November 5, 2026, the Trump administration filed a notification with the federal court that construction would begin immediately. Related: The Archvillain and His Arch: Trump Builds for the Ages That notification was followed within minutes by a 33-page injunction from U.S. District Judge Tanya S. Chutkan to stop any construction for 14 days while the court continues to consider challenges to the legality of the monument. Judge Chutkan wrote, “[T]he District and Virginia have offered enough proof “indicating that the harm is certain to occur in the near future” to show irreparable harm.” She also wrote that “the most straightforward of Congress’s planning directives,” remains in force today. Now codified at 40 U.S.C. § 8106, the statute provides in full: “A building or structure shall not be erected on any reservation, park, or public grounds of the Federal Government in the District of Columbia without express authority of Congress.” Reasons to Stop the Arch More than 131 members of the public, including architects, historians and military veterans, demanded that the monument proposal be stopped as it would: Destroy the silence and solemnity of nearby Arlington National Cemetery Be an affront due to Trump’s racist comments toward people and countries of color to the connections from Arlington House of the Confederacy through Memorial Circle, across Memorial Bridge to the Union’s Lincoln Memorial, an area that is the symbol of reunification of the United States after the Civil War to free African-American slaves from the horrific inhumanity of others (the history of which Trump is attempting to change in the Smithsonian Museum of American History) Be an affront to military members whom 5 times Vietnam draft deferment Trump has called “losers and suckers” Would cost billions of dollars when the nation has dramatic human needs instead of a monument to the narcissism and ego of one President Would be a hazard to aircraft approaching National airport no matter what the politicized current leadership of the FAA says (just ask the pilots on the next flight you take into National airport) Would disrupt rush-hour traffic into and out of Washington, DC for years (Over 27,000 vehicles, 1,100 cyclists, and 1,200 pedestrians pass by Memorial Circle on an average workday) Would become an unnecessary target in the nation’s capital as a well-publicized by Trump as storage depot for munitions and drones Trump proposes to also have snipers on the top of the monument, snipers who I fear would decimate the flocks of geese that routinely fly into Memorial circle no doubt considered by snipers as enemy drones approaching the monument, not to mention “suspect” citizens who may approach the monument We need more citizens standing up and standing with us at Memorial Circle each day. 4-6pm Vigil Each workday from 7-9am and 4-6pm, residents from Northern Virginia, the District of Columbia and Maryland come to Memorial Circle (Metro Blue line to Arlington Cemetery) to hold signs to “Stop the Arch.” Please join us to see the beautiful sunrise over the Potomac in the 7am vigil and the colorful autumn colors of the trees along the Potomac in the sunset during the afternoon 4-6pm vigil . Tens of thousands of our fellow residents travel through Memorial Circle in the morning and afternoon rush hour traffic—and you will be rewarded with thousands of honking horns showing support for Stopping the Arch!!! Ask Your Congressional Representative to Sign On! Representative Don Beyers from Northern Virginia already has 80 co-sponsors of House Resolution H.R. 9047 to stop the Arch. Call your representative and ask her/him to sign on.

articles.title: Paraguay Political, Financial Crisis: the Liberal Economic Model Continues to Fail
articles.author: Thania Saucedo
articles.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Paraguay is undergoing one of the most significant political and financial crises in its recent history. The Central Bank of Paraguay’s intervention in Ueno Bank —following the detection of serious irregularities in its operations and solvency issues—triggered a crisis that quickly expanded beyond the banking sector. Today, it has direct consequences for the government of Santiago Peña and has triggered an impeachment process that calls into question the very future of the president himself. To understand what is happening, it is necessary to explain a few key points. Ueno Bank experienced exponential growth in recent years, coinciding with the start of Santiago Peña’s administration. It grew to have nearly three million customers—more than 50 percent of the country’s adult population—and received approximately $800 million in deposits from the public sector. Among these funds are those linked to the Social Security Institute (IPS), which administers the retirement and health contributions of thousands of workers. Related: Latin America’s Far-Right Turn: Authoritarianism, Austerity and the New Oligarchy One of the problems is that the president himself maintained business ties with the group associated with the bank until March 2025. Added to this is the fact that Carlos Carvallo, who had served as president of Financiera Ueno, subsequently went on to head the Central Bank, the agency responsible for supervising and regulating the financial system. During this administration, provisions designed to prevent this type of conflict of interest—known as “revolving door” regulations—were also amended. The bank’s intervention, the freezing of deposits, and investigations into loans granted to companies linked to its owners ultimately exposed a web of relationships between private interests and public institutions. However, beyond the numbers and financial transactions, there are thousands of people who today cannot access their savings ; workers facing uncertainty about their wages; and retirees whose financial resources are at risk. Financial inclusion, which was touted as one of the great achievements of the economic model, ultimately turned into a massive scam against the population. Santiago Peña’s ties to the business group, the decisions made by the executive branch, and the responsibilities of the oversight agencies are among the issues that gave rise to the impeachment request. The opposition spearheaded the process in Congress, and on 5 November, the Chamber of Deputies approved the charges against the president . Peña submitted his resignation, but both chambers rejected this attempt to step down, and the Senate proceeded with the process. At the time of this writing, the president is set to present his defense in the impeachment trial. However, to understand this crisis, one must also look to the National Republican Association (ANR), the Colorado Party , – deeply entrenched in the Paraguayan state apparatus and linked to Alfredo Stroessner’s 35-year dictatorship – and particularly to Horacio Cartes (HC). Paraguay has a political peculiarity that is fundamental to understanding what is happening. The Colorado Party has governed virtually uninterrupted since 1947; the only interruption in that long cycle was the administration of Fernando Lugo (2008–2012), who came to power leading an alliance that managed to defeat the Colorado Party at the polls after more than six decades. However, his administration came to an abrupt end in June 2012 through a parliamentary coup that removed him from office in just 48 hours via a controversial impeachment trial. For social movements and sectors of the popular base, this event was not just another episode in history but a political operation orchestrated by sectors of the Paraguayan right, with Horacio Cartes as one of its main actors and with alleged complicity and support from external interests, including those of the U.S. Embassy. Currently, power within the ANR is fiercely contested by internal factions, but the Cartes faction (HC) has become the ruling party’s main power base. Cartes was not only president of the Republic from 2013 to 2018 but subsequently assumed the presidency of the Colorado Party itself and maintained enormous influence over the decisions of Santiago Peña’s government. Peña rose to the presidency with Cartes’ political backing. His candidacy and subsequent administration were built under the leadership of the Honor Colorado movement. For this reason, what we are seeing today involves a major political contradiction: the very same faction that built and sustained this administration has now decided to support the impeachment proceedings against the president. Cartes’ position shifted as the crisis unfolded. Initially, his inner circle rejected the possibility of impeachment and sought to pin the blame on Central Bank officials. However, on 5 November, Cartes publicly announced that the ANR would support Peña’s impeachment. This move cannot be interpreted simply as an institutional decision by the Colorado Party; it also reflects a struggle for political control, for the continuity of the government’s agenda, and for the preservation of a power structure that the movement itself helped build. Against this backdrop, social movements and the popular sector are not limiting their criticism to demanding individual accountability and rejecting any attempt at impunity; they are also warning that this crisis is yet another example of the failure of the liberal economic model, which for years insisted that the market could regulate itself, that the state should reduce its intervention, and that privatization and deregulation were the path to development. They promised that, if we let capital operate freely, wealth would eventually reach the entire population, that economic growth would translate into well-being, and that everyone would benefit from this supposed trickle-down effect. In Paraguay today, the consequences are felt by every worker, as a result of financial narco-capitalism. This is a model that unscrupulously manages public resources, concentrates wealth, and fosters ties between political power and private interests. It is a system in which profits remain in the hands of certain sectors, while the consequences of their operations ultimately fall on the population. Therefore, what is happening on this side of the southern part of our America is not isolated from what is happening in other parts of the world; it is part of a dynamic in which big capital dictates political decisions, appropriates the commons, and turns basic rights and needs into business opportunities. The settings change, the actors change, but the logic remains the same. However, the evident failure of the economic policy of financial capitalism also opens up an opportunity for the organized popular movement: to envision a different future and build a political and economic alternative that breaks with this logic—to pave the way toward a world in which the economy serves life rather than the accumulation of wealth by a few, and in which people can decide on their resources, their present, and their destiny.
